# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
**40,000 users | Dual-run architecture (old + new systems operating concurrently)**
**Prepared:** 2026-09-13

---

## 1. Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in four phased batches. Because both systems can run simultaneously, the strategy is: migrate a batch → run both systems in shadow/parallel for that batch → validate financial parity → proceed to the next batch. The old billing system remains fully operational through the entire migration and is only considered for retirement in a separate phase after all users are confirmed migrated and stable.

---

## 2. Phased Rollout

### Phase 1 — Canary (0.25% of users, ~100 users)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration/regression test suite in staging; a rollback script has been tested end-to-end in staging (migrate → rollback → verify original state restored); on-call rotation and dashboards for the new system are live; internal employee/test accounts (not counted in the 100) have run through the new system for at least 5 business days with zero critical defects.

**Population:** Internal employees and opted-in low-risk external users with simple billing profiles (single currency, no active disputes, no complex proration/credits).

**Duration:** Minimum 3 business days of parallel run before evaluating exit criteria.

---

### Phase 2 — Early Adopters (5% of users, ~2,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full parallel-run window with zero unresolved billing discrepancies (see Section 4 metric); rollback tested successfully at least once on a real Phase 1 account; support team has documented and closed all Phase 1 tickets; change advisory board sign-off obtained.

**Population:** A randomized, representative slice across plan types, geographies, and payment methods (cards, ACH, invoicing) — deliberately broader than Phase 1 to surface edge cases (multi-currency, coupons, proration, dunning states).

**Duration:** Minimum 5 business days of parallel run before evaluating exit criteria.

---

### Phase 3 — General Rollout (35% of users, ~14,000 users, cumulative ~40%)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 discrepancy rate remains below halt threshold (Section 4) for its entire duration; customer support ticket volume attributable to billing migration is at or below Phase 2 baseline; infrastructure load testing confirms the new system handles at least 3x the concurrent transaction volume of this phase's user count; finance team has reconciled Phase 2 revenue/invoicing against the old system with no unexplained variance.

**Population:** Remaining users segmented in waves by geography/timezone (to keep support coverage aligned with active hours), excluding the most complex enterprise/custom-contract accounts, which are reserved for Phase 4.

**Duration:** Rolled out in sub-waves of ~5% every 2–3 days, each sub-wave gated on the same discrepancy metric before the next sub-wave begins.

---

### Phase 4 — Full Migration / Long Tail (59.75% of users, ~23,900 users, cumulative 100%)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative discrepancy rate below threshold; zero open Sev-1/Sev-2 billing incidents; finance sign-off on reconciliation for all prior phases; dedicated migration runbooks prepared for known complex accounts (enterprise contracts, custom pricing, multi-entity billing).

**Population:** All remaining users, including the highest-complexity accounts, migrated last and with white-glove support/manual verification for enterprise contracts.

**Note on decommissioning:** Retirement, disabling, or decommissioning of the old billing system is explicitly **out of scope for Phase 4** and is not proposed to begin until a separate, subsequent **Phase 5 — Legacy Decommission** phase, which starts only after all 40,000 users have been on the new system for a defined stabilization period (minimum 30 days) with clean reconciliation and no rollback events. Phase 5 is not part of the user-migration percentage count above (0 users are migrated in Phase 5).

---

## 3. Rollback Strategy

- Every phase supports per-batch rollback: because both systems run concurrently, an affected batch can be flipped back to the old system as the source of truth without impacting other batches.
- Rollback is triggered automatically if the Section 4 halt metric is breached, and manually by the on-call lead or migration owner at any time.
- Rolled-back users remain on the old system until root cause is identified and a fix is validated in staging; they re-enter the rollout in a later sub-wave, not automatically retried.

---

## 4. Halt Metric

**Automatic rollout halt condition:** If the billing discrepancy rate (transactions where new-system output — amount charged, invoice total, or tax calculation — differs from old-system output by more than $0.01 or 0.1%, whichever is greater) exceeds **0.5% of transactions processed by the currently active phase within any rolling 24-hour window**, the rollout is halted immediately: no further users are migrated into the next batch/sub-wave, and the migration owner and finance lead are paged.

Additional halt/pause triggers (non-numeric but tracked alongside):
- Any single Sev-1 incident (customers double-charged or failed critical payments) — halts immediately regardless of rate.
- Customer support ticket volume for billing issues exceeds 2x the pre-migration 7-day baseline for the affected cohort.

---

## 5. Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double charges occur when both systems attempt to process the same billing cycle for a migrated user | Implement an idempotency lock/flag per account that marks which system is authoritative for billing at any given time, verified before any charge is executed | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new systems for payment method tokens, credits, or subscription state during the parallel-run window | Run a continuous automated reconciliation job comparing account state every 15 minutes for all migrated accounts and alert on any mismatch | Data Integrity / Reconciliation Team Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contracts or complex proration rules are miscalculated by the new system, causing revenue leakage or customer disputes | Reserve all complex/custom-contract accounts for Phase 4, require manual finance review and sign-off before migrating each such account | Finance Operations Lead
RISK: Migration tooling or scripts fail partway through a batch, leaving users in an inconsistent state between systems | Design all migration steps to be idempotent and resumable, with a pre-migration snapshot taken for every account to enable point-in-time restore | Migration Platform Engineer
RISK: Customer support is unprepared for new-system-specific issues, leading to poor customer experience and escalations | Train support staff on new system behavior before each phase, provide a phase-specific runbook and escalation path, and staff up during each parallel-run window | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Regulatory/tax compliance calculations differ between old and new systems in specific jurisdictions | Run jurisdiction-specific tax calculation parity tests in staging before Phase 3 (broad geographic rollout) and flag any jurisdiction with variance for manual review before inclusion | Compliance & Tax Lead

---

## 6. Post-Migration (Out of Scope for This Rollout)

Legacy system decommissioning is a separate, subsequent initiative (Phase 5) requiring its own risk assessment, data archival plan, and stakeholder sign-off, and must not begin until the 30-day stabilization window following 100% migration (Phase 4) has passed with no rollbacks and clean financial reconciliation.

---

PHASES: 4
